problem: The existing relationship graph was commercially underused because company trigger materialization correctly required explicit trigger evidence.
decision: Use Powerhouse itself as the canonical relationship intelligence and scoring layer. Public web is the second evidence layer; Apollo and other vendors are optional fallback only.
prevention_rule: Never make a vendor the canonical sales brain. Relationship warmth is not a buying trigger. Use bounded internal research to create evidence, and keep unsolicited external outreach human-authorized.
root_cause: Powerhouse already held a large first-party relationship graph and company/person intelligence, but the commercial runtime only materialized companies with explicit buying-trigger evidence. High-value relationships without a current trigger therefore remained commercially idle and could tempt an unnecessary vendor-first enrichment design.
prevention: Powerhouse first-party evidence is always the canonical source for relationship scoring.
Use bounded public-web evidence only to close concrete freshness, company-identity, role or signal gaps.
Apollo/Lusha/ZoomInfo or similar vendors are optional fallback only and never required runtime dependencies or canonical truth.
Relationship warmth is not a buying trigger.
Unsolicited external outreach remains human-authorized; autonomous work is internal research and evidence enrichment.
Execute bounded internal relationship research automatically against canonical public evidence stores before trigger materialization; do not leave autonomous-safe research as advice-only work.

A selected relationship research action must not remain a dead-end queue item: execute existing-evidence matching automatically and dispatch bounded public research from the existing commercial scheduler.
